# Starter Kits

<div class="pb-banner pb-c-build" markdown>
<div class="pb-banner-text" markdown>
<span class="pb-banner-kicker">For everyone</span>

**Get every team building in the first hour.**
</div>
![](../assets/img/pencil-blue.png)
</div>

A starter kit gets every team from "we have an idea" to "we're building" in the first hour. It's a public repo that teams star, read, and build from.

**For partners:** contributing a starter kit (sample data, an API quickstart, or a template repo with your tools pre-configured) is one of the most effective ways to get strong work on your challenge. Teams spend the weekend on your problem instead of on setup.

## What goes in a starter kit

| Section | What it contains |
|---|---|
| The challenge | The brief or track, in the repo, not only on a website |
| Getting started | Accounts, credits, and tool setup, step by step |
| Solution ideas | Prompts to think with, framed as *Who / What / How*, never the answer |
| Architecture | An example diagram of how the pieces could fit, clearly marked as one option |
| Resources | Datasets, APIs, tutorials, and labs, with approximate times |
| Submission | The checklist, deadline, and where to submit |
| Rules and guides | Official rules, the hackathon guide, and the Code of Conduct |
| Workshop decks | Slides from the event workshops |

## Starter kits from past events

| Kit | Event | Highlights |
|---|---|---|
| [A2Tech360 Hackathon Starter Kit](https://github.com/A2Tech360/a2tech360-hackathon) | A2Tech360 / JacHacks A2Tech 2026 | Local Impact worksheet, IBM and Google credit guides, GitHub org with AI code review |
| [Call for Code: Zero Hunger](https://github.com/Call-for-Code/Solution-Starter-Kit-Hunger-2021) | Call for Code 2021 | Problem background, architecture diagram, Who/What/How solution ideas, Node-RED lab |
| [UF Hacks Starter Kit](https://github.com/jritten/UF_Hacks_Starter_Kit) | UF Hacks | Save Energy campaign with a React starter app and workshop tutorial |
| [IBM x SiB workshop series](https://github.com/jritten/ibm-x-sib) | Partner workshop series | Event streaming and containerized deployment, local to cloud |

## Tips

- Keep the brief and the rules in the repo so teams have one place to look.
- Offer ideas as questions. The moment a kit prescribes the solution, every team builds the same thing.
- Make the kit a GitHub template repository so teams can start their own repo with one click.
